related_questions.question: What are the disadvantages of monoclonal antibodies?

text_blocks.snippet: Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), while effective in treating various diseases, do have potential drawbacks. These include side effects, high costs, and limitations in accessing certain tissues. Some specific disadvantages are:
snippet_highlighted_words: side effects, high costs, and limitations in accessing certain tissues

list.title: Hypersensitivity reactions:
list.snippet: Allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, can occur, particularly during the initial infusion.

list.title: Infusion-related reactions:
list.snippet: Some patients experience fever, chills, or other symptoms during or shortly after the infusion.

list.title: Organ-specific toxicities:
list.snippet: Certain mAbs can cause problems in specific organs, such as cardiotoxicity with trastuzumab or skin rashes with cetuximab.

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: mAbs can increase the risk of infections due to their immunosuppressive effects, potentially reactivating latent infections like tuberculosis.

list.title: Immune-related adverse events:
list.snippet: mAbs can trigger immune responses, including cytokine release syndrome, which can be severe.

list.title: Cardiovascular issues:
list.snippet: Some mAbs have been linked to high blood pressure, heart failure, or blood clots.

list.title: Skin problems:
list.snippet: Rashes, sores, and other skin issues can occur.

list.title: Cost:
list.snippet: Monoclonal antibodies can be very expensive, making them inaccessible to some patients, especially those without insurance.

list.title: Accessibility:
list.snippet: mAbs may have difficulty reaching certain tissues, like tumors in solid organs, limiting their effectiveness.

list.title: Production challenges:
list.snippet: Producing mAbs can be complex and require specialized facilities and skilled personnel.

list.title: Potential for immunogenicity:
list.snippet: The body may develop antibodies against the monoclonal antibody itself, reducing its effectiveness or causing adverse reactions.

list.title: Limited efficacy:
list.snippet: mAbs are not always effective, and their success can vary depending on the specific disease and patient.
